messages:
david: Heads-up — I just applied a terraform change that moved the IAM role binding for the service account 'payment-uploader' into the tenant module. Now a few pods in payments-staging can't access S3 creds. Anyone seen service-account / annotation shadowing before?
sofia: Which annotation did you change? IRSA uses eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn — did you accidentally set it on the namespace instead of the SA, or change the projected token config?
david: @sofia good call. I updated our k8s module to annotate SAs via for_each. snippet from TF plan: ```hcl resource "kubernetes_service_account" "sa" { for_each = var.sas metadata { name = each.key namespace = each.value.namespace annotations = each.value.annotations } } ``` I added the IRSA arn to annotations map.
maria: Quick theory: if the namespace also had some iam annotations we might be fighting a controller or mutating webhook that applies a different role. Can you paste the SA YAML + namespace annotations?
david: SA YAML (redacted): ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: payment-uploader namespace: payments-staging annotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/payment-uploader-role ``` Namespace annotations: `env: staging`, no iam-related keys.
sofia: Huh — if namespace has no conflicting keys then likely pods have old tokens cached. Kubelet token projected files are renewed, but many apps read token only at startup. Deleting the pod should pick up the new SA annotation role via IRSA. Did you try restarting pods?
david: I tried deleting one pod, it picked up creds properly. Doing a RollingUpdate on the deployment only replaced some pods; others stuck in CrashLoop and then picked up later.
maria: That behavior is consistent with controller sync timing + the way our deploys create pods fast. Safe remediation steps I recommend: 1) patch the SA directly with kubectl so infra and TF match (kubectl -n payments-staging patch sa payment-uploader -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":"arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/payment-uploader-role"}}}'), 2) rollout restart deployment/payment-uploader -n payments-staging, 3) verify token audience/role via `kubectl exec` into new pod and check `/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token` headers via `curl -sS --header 'Authorization: Bearer $(cat /var/run/secrets...token)' http://169.254.169.253/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials` (or use aws sts get-caller-identity with the token to confirm role).
sofia: Also ensure TF state didn't create a duplicate SA in another namespace with same name. We had a bug where module path changed and created an extra SA in tenant ns which confused teams. Run `kubectl get sa --all-namespaces | grep payment-uploader` to double-check.
david: Ran that — only exists in payments-staging. I'll patch and restart, then run a smoke test against S3.
ci-bot: terraform plan finished (workspace=prod) — no drift detected for k8s module.
ops-bot: Noted for rotation tracking. Incident T-444 created for credential rotation fallout, tagging @oncall.
david: Patch + rollout started. I'll post back with success/fail. :thumbsup:
sofia: Thanks — if anything weird pops up ping me and i'll help debug the token inside a pod.
maria: If this recurs we should add a pre-rollout check in our deployment pipeline: confirm SA annotation present and pods mount tokens with the right aud claim before cutover.
david: Agreed — filing a follow-up PR for pipeline gate after I confirm this is resolved.
